Smart Patient Monitoring System

A sensor-based patient monitoring prototype designed to track body temperature and heartbeat, evaluate readings against predefined conditions, and trigger an alert when potentially abnormal readings are detected.

MY CONTRIBUTION
Programming + Hardware Wiring
APPROACH
Integrated an Arduino Uno with an LM35 temperature sensor and heartbeat sensor, then implemented logic to collect and evaluate readings.
OUTCOME
A prototype demonstrating the interaction between hardware sensors, embedded programming, real-time readings, and an alert mechanism.
SMARTCARE / CASE STUDY

From sensing to real-time patient alerts.

01 — PROBLEM

Basic health monitoring can require continuous observation of vital readings. The goal was to create a compact system capable of monitoring body temperature and heartbeat and providing an immediate warning when potentially abnormal conditions occur.

02 — SOLUTION

SmartCare uses an Arduino Uno to collect temperature and heartbeat readings through connected sensors. The readings are evaluated against predefined conditions, and the buzzer is triggered when an alert condition is detected.

03 — MY ROLE

I worked on programming and hardware wiring, including connecting the sensors to the Arduino Uno, implementing the monitoring logic, and integrating the buzzer as the alert mechanism.

04 — TECHNOLOGIES

Arduino Uno · Arduino IDE · LM35 Temperature Sensor · Heartbeat Sensor · Buzzer · Embedded Programming

05 — SYSTEM FLOW

Sense → Sensors collect temperature and heartbeat readings.

Analyze → Arduino processes the readings against predefined conditions.

Alert → The buzzer provides a warning when the defined conditions are met.

06 — OUTCOME

Developed a working prototype demonstrating the interaction between hardware sensors, embedded programming, real-time readings, conditional logic, and an automated alert mechanism.

07 — WHAT I LEARNED

The project strengthened my understanding of sensor integration, hardware-software interaction, embedded programming, conditional logic, troubleshooting, and practical problem solving.
